title: An AI breast-cancer screening system evaluated in two countries
summary: Among 25,856 women in the UK and 3,097 in the US, the system reduced false positives by 5.7% (US) and 1.2% (UK), and false negatives by 9.4% and 2.7% in absolute terms compared with radiologists. Trained only on UK data, it also outperformed specialists on US data. Retrospective evaluation (Nature): prospective studies are needed, and clinical deployment is unclear.
organization: Google DeepMind, Google Health, Cancer Research UK Imperial Centre, and Northwestern University

evidence.tested: Retrospective evaluation on UK (25,856 women) and US (3,097 women) screening mammograms, compared with individual radiologists' decisions; a reader study and a simulated double-reading workflow were also run.
evidence.unknown: The authors state prospective studies are required and that how to deploy the system clinically is not yet determined; the US data were enriched; the second-reader scenario was only simulated.
evidence.ai_role: Predicted from screening mammograms alone whether a biopsy would later show cancer.
